title: normalize rate-limit headers and error mapping in OpenAI adapter
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Normalize incoming rate-limit headers from various providers into a single internal contract. Map vendor-specific 429 payloads to Redwood's standard error schema for predictable client handling. Backwards-compatible changes only.
description: Motivation: the OpenAI-compat adapter sees a wide variety of rate-limit headers and 429 error payloads from models/proxies in the wild. Clients (and our retry/fallback logic) need a single, predictable contract to make robust retry decisions and to emit consistent telemetry. This PR normalizes common rate-limit headers (Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Reset, RateLimit-Remaining variants) into a clear internal RateLimitInfo structure, and canonicalizes 429 and related error payloads into Redwood's error schema (code, reason, retry_after_seconds, scope). It also clarifies idempotency semantics for streaming/function-call requests: streaming responses that are aborted by client disconnect now surface a consistent retryable flag and a recommended backoff hint when we can infer a server-side retry-after. Changes: 1) openai_adapter/headers_normalizer.py: new utility that parses multiple header formats and returns RateLimitInfo. 2) openai_adapter/error_mapper.py: maps vendor error shapes into redwood error codes like RATE_LIMIT, THROTTLED, BAD_REQUEST and includes retry_after_seconds when available. 3) openai_adapter/streaming_guard.py: ensures idempotency-key and request fingerprint are included in logs and in the mapped error payload for streaming aborts and connection resets. 4) tests/*: unit and integration tests covering header permutations, streaming aborts, and adapter fallback to internal backoff logic. 5) docs/adapters/openai-rate-limits.md: short reference of header variants and recommended client behavior. Backwards compatibility: adapter emits the same HTTP responses to external callers but augments error JSON with standardized fields where possible; no public API contract change. Why not earlier approaches: previous heuristics were scattered and added flaky behavior in autoscaling canaries where transient 429s were misinterpreted. This centralization reduces duplicate parsing logic and yields cleaner metrics for rate-limit incidents. Rollout plan: feature gated via env var OPENAI_ADAPTER_NORMALIZE_HEADERS=false by default; flip on after staged canary for one week. See linked Linear tasks for SLO & dashboard updates.
